title: Composition on the image
statement: Let $M$ and $U$ be finite Turing machines over the binary alphabet, let $f,g$ be functions from binary strings to binary strings, and let $T_1,T_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. Suppose $M$ computes $f$ on every input $x$ within $T_1(|x|)$ steps, and $U$ computes $g(x)$ from input $f(x)$ within $T_2(|x|)$ steps for every $x$. Then there is a finite Turing machine that computes $g$ on every input within $2T_1(n)+T_2(n)+2$ steps on inputs of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ and $U$ are finite Turing machines over the binary alphabet
$U$ computes $g(x)$ from $f(x)$ within $T_2(|x|)$ steps for every $x$
replaced:
Let $M$ and $U$ be finite multi-tape Turing machines over the binary alphabet, let
$f, g$ be functions on binary strings and $T_1, T_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ time
bounds. If $M$ computes $f$ within $T_1$, and for every input $x$ the machine $U$ run
on $f(x)$ halts within $T_2(|x|)$ steps with output $g(x)$, then some finite machine
computes $g$ within time $n \mapsto 2\,T_1(n) + T_2(n) + 2$.
